answer:
ANSWER: About 38% of the miRNAs — 67 of 175 = 38.29% (38.2857%) — show significant differential expression between DM1 patients (P_1..P_10, n=10) and controls (C_11..C_20, n=10) before multiple-testing correction. Spec: two-sided Student's independent-samples t-test (scipy.stats.ttest_ind, equal_var=True) on raw Ct per miRNA, pairwise deletion of the 22 literal "NAN" cells, strict uncorrected p < 0.05. Reproduce with `python3 work/analysis.py`; `work/verify_from_csv.py` independently re-derives 67/175 = 38.2857%.

1) HEADLINE DETAIL
- Numerator 67, denominator 175 (all unique miRNA rows; no filtering, none dropped), percentage 38.29%.
- 0 NaN p-values (min per-group n = 7), so all 175 rows were testable.
- Direction: 66 of the 67 significant miRNAs have lower mean Ct in patients (higher circulating expression in DM1); 1 has higher Ct.

2) SENSITIVITY GRID (denominator 175 unless noted)
- PRIMARY Student's t, raw Ct: 67 = 38.29%
- Welch t (equal_var=False): 63 = 36.00%
- Mann-Whitney U (two-sided): 59 = 33.71%
- Student t excluding Ct >= 35 cells: 65 = 37.14%
- Student t on 2^-Ct: 54 = 30.86%
- Variant, complete-case miRNAs only (161): 63 = 39.13%
The count is NOT unchanged across tests: 59-67 (33.7-38.3%) for the three location tests, 54-67 including the scale/near-negative variants. Sign and ranking of the strongest hits are identical everywhere; the spread comes only from calls sitting on the 0.05 line.

3) P-VALUE DISTRIBUTION (primary)
- p<0.0001: 0 (0.00%) | p<0.001: 4 (2.29%) | p<0.01: 32 (18.29%) | p<0.05: 67 (38.29%) | p<0.10: 88 (50.29%) | max p = 0.976.
- Smallest p: hsa-miR-20b 3.23e-04; hsa-miR-92a 6.86e-04; hsa-miR-222 8.19e-04; hsa-miR-1974 8.29e-04; hsa-miR-532-5p 1.06e-03; hsa-miR-130a 1.16e-03; hsa-miR-30e 1.27e-03; hsa-miR-106b* 1.42e-03; hsa-miR-486-5p 1.74e-03; hsa-miR-30b 1.76e-03; hsa-miR-107 2.36e-03; hsa-miR-34a 2.48e-03 (patient-minus-control ΔCt ≈ -1.1 to -2.1 cycles).
- Borderline density: 16 of the 67 significant calls fall in p=[0.03,0.05) and 15 non-significant miRNAs fall in [0.05,0.08) — 31 miRNAs in the 0.03-0.08 band. So ~24% of the headline set is within 0.02 of the cutoff; the result is a soft-edged count, not a cliff, but it is not driven by a couple of calls.

4) FLIPS
Student vs Welch — 4 flips, all sig→ns, all borderline (0.047-0.048 → 0.050-0.054): hsa-let-7d* (0.0470→0.0542), hsa-miR-27a (0.0471→0.0514), hsa-miR-99b (0.0471→0.0521), hsa-miR-885-5p (0.0474→0.0500). No ns→sig; Welch is uniformly slightly conservative because control SDs exceed patient SDs.
Student vs Mann-Whitney — 12 flips, all borderline:
  sig→ns: hsa-let-7b (0.0413→0.1041), hsa-let-7d* (0.0470→0.1041), hsa-miR-10a (0.0497→0.0550), hsa-miR-151-5p (0.0364→0.0640), hsa-miR-26a (0.0415→0.1041), hsa-miR-27a (0.0471→0.0890), hsa-miR-30e* (0.0350→0.0757), hsa-miR-495 (0.0415→0.0640), hsa-miR-99a (0.0495→0.1041), hsa-miR-99b (0.0471→0.0539).
  ns→sig: hsa-miR-125a-5p (0.0699→0.0376), hsa-miR-320b (0.0565→0.0452).
  (The repeated MW p=0.1041 reflects the coarse achievable-p lattice at n=10 vs 10 with ties — rank tests are visibly underpowered here.)
Student vs Ct≥35-excluded — 4 flips: hsa-miR-501-3p (0.0194→0.1443) and hsa-miR-92b (0.1911→0.0108) are NOT borderline (genuinely driven by near-negative cells); hsa-miR-10a (0.0497→0.3095) and hsa-miR-885-5p (0.0474→0.1366) borderline.
Student vs 2^-Ct — 17 flips, 13 borderline; non-borderline losses hsa-miR-142-5p (0.0147→0.1873) and hsa-miR-199a-5p (0.0250→0.1060) come from skew induced by 2^-Ct, which is why raw Ct remained the primary scale.
No multiple-testing correction was computed as the answer (out of scope).

payload.headline: 67 of 175 = 38.29%
payload.test: two-sided Student's independent-samples t-test on raw Ct (scipy.stats.ttest_ind, equal_var=True), pairwise deletion of literal NAN cells, raw p<0.05
